summary.name: Systems Performance: Enterprise and the Cloud
summary.one_liner: A sample PDF excerpt (front matter, table of contents, and chapter outline) from Brendan Gregg's book on operating system and systems performance analysis, published by Pearson in 2014.
use_cases: finding CPU performance tools such as uptime, vmstat, mpstat and perf
understanding the USE method for resource analysis
reference reading for SRE and performance engineers
planning a performance investigation of enterprise or cloud servers
summary.what_it_does: The page is a sample PDF from the book Systems Performance: Enterprise and the Cloud, containing the copyright and publishing front matter, the full table of contents, and the chapter 6 CPUs sample. The table of contents outlines topics such as methodology (USE method, drill-down analysis, latency analysis, scientific method), observability sources and tracing tools (DTrace, SystemTap, perf), and per-resource chapters covering CPUs, memory, file systems, disks, and networks. The CPU chapter listed for this sample covers CPU architecture, run queues, utilization and saturation, and analysis tools such as uptime, vmstat, mpstat, top, pidstat, DTrace, and perf. The extracted text itself contains only the front matter and contents, not the full chapter body.
notable: Written by Brendan Gregg, known for performance tooling work
Covers Solaris-based and Linux-based kernels and tools
Includes detailed methodology sections such as the USE method and anti-methods
Sample PDF offers the CPUs chapter as a free excerpt
caveats: Only a sample excerpt; the full book is required for complete content
Extracted text contains front matter and table of contents, not the CPU chapter body
Book is from 2014 and tool coverage reflects that era (e.g. Solaris tools such as prstat and mdb)
